newsitem.title: FINLAND: OKOBANK SEES MARKKA-ERM LINK AFTER LOCAL ELECTIONS.
newsitem.headline: OKOBANK SEES MARKKA-ERM LINK AFTER LOCAL ELECTIONS.

text.p: A link of the Finnish markka to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) would be justified after the October 20 elections, OKOBANK chief economist Matti Huomo said on Monday.
"Our view has been that it would be justified to link the markka after the municipal elections," Huomo told a news conference, adding he still stood by that view.
The postponement last spring of a markka-ERM link was due to political pressures related to the local elections, Huomo said.
Huomo said the markka would be pegged close to the exchange rates prevaling at the time of the fixing.

"I agree with Lipponen that the markka will be linked close to the rate it has been trading at in the days prior to a fixing," he said, referring to Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's view that there would be little scope for manipulation when setting central parity exchange rates for the markka in ERM.
"According to inflation, purchase power parity or the economy's external balance it is hard to interpret whether the Finnish markka is clearly over- or undervalued," Huomo said.
Last week, OKOBANK said in a bond market review that Finland should not make a hasty decision to link the markka to ERM.
"While parliaments in Germany, France and many other EU countries are discussing their next year's budgets, it is not wise to make hasty decision regarding the ERM link," the review said.
"It would not be wise to be too active before the big decisions in the other EU-countries (1997 budgets) are finalised," Huomo said.
